Let me analyze this conflict.

Axis: applicant
- Register: "Durukan Teknik Olcu ve Tarti Aletleri Sanayi ve Ticaret Ltd. Sti"
- Document: "Durukan Teknik Ölçü ve Tartı Aletleri Sanayi ve Ticaret Ltd. Şti"

The register version is the ASCII-folded version (Turkish characters stripped: Ölçü → Olcu, Tartı → Tarti, Şti → Sti). The document version has proper Turkish diacritics.

Per the rules: "spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity." This is clearly an accent difference — the same Turkish company name, one ASCII-normalized, one with proper diacritics.

Verdict: same-entity. Best value: which one? The rules say for same-entity accent differences, we should pick... The rules don't explicitly say which value for same-entity in general — only for number/year format differences it says "with the register's canonical form." For applicant, the document is the legal instrument and carries the accurate accented form. The best fused value should be the document's properly accented Turkish name since it's the legal instrument and the accurate rendering. The register value is just an ASCII transliteration (likely from the OIML-CS database which strips non-ASCII). Since the certificate is the legal instrument and the document form is more accurate (proper Turkish orthography), best_value = document value.

Verdict: same-entity, best_value: "Durukan Teknik Ölçü ve Tartı Aletleri Sanayi ve Ticaret Ltd. Şti", why: accent/ASCII-fold difference of the same Turkish company name; document preserves correct diacritics on the legal instrument.
